sources.entry: espanso - Cross-platform Text Expander, a powerful replacement for Alfred Snippets

summary.one_liner: espanso is a cross-platform text expander written in Rust that replaces typed keywords with predefined text, snippets, emojis, or script output.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes espanso as a program that detects when a specific keyword is typed and replaces it with something else, working system-wide across Windows, macOS, and Linux. Matches are defined in YAML files, and the README gives an example mapping a trigger like ":hello" to a replacement string. It lists support for emoji, image expansion, date expansion, custom scripts, shell commands, regex triggers, and forms. A built-in package manager installs packages from the espanso hub, and configuration can be made app-specific. A search bar feature is also mentioned. The README states the project is privacy-first and runs 100% locally.
use_cases: expand frequently typed sentences or phrases
insert emojis by typing a keyword
run custom scripts or shell commands from a trigger
set up system-wide autocorrect for common typos
notable: Cross-platform text expander with file-based YAML configuration
Built-in package manager connected to the espanso hub
Supports regex triggers, forms, date expansion, and shell command output
Privacy-first, runs locally with no tracking per the README
caveats: Wayland support is described as experimental
Donation options are listed as PayPal, with another option marked coming soon; no paid tiers are named
